(Order of the Court was made by J.NISHA BANU, J.)

This writ petition is filed for a Mandamus,
directing the 4th respondent to consider the petitioner's representation dated 15.05.2025, and to take action to demolish the illegal and unauthorised construction put up by the 6th respondent on the land bearing SF No.393/2 situate at Anupparpalayam Village, Coimbatore Town, Coimbatore,
located at the address Door No.40, Senguptha Street, Ram Nagar, Coimbatore, without any building approval and planning https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 15/07/2025 01:31:06 pm )
permission and in violation of the provisions of Tamil Nadu Combined Development Building Rules 2019 and Tamil Nadu Town and Country Planning Act, 1971, within a time as fixed by this Court.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that he is the owner and occupier of the the residential premises bearing Door No.41, Senguptha Street, Ramnagar, Coimbatore-641 009, situated in T.S No.393,
Anupparpalayam Village, Coimbatore.

The 6th respondent is the owner of the adjacent property in T.S.No.393/2 and is presently carrying out large scale construction activities with a proposed built-up area exceeding 2000 square feet, without obtaining any sanction or approval from the competent authorities.

The said construction is being undertaken without leaving the mandatory side setbacks and rear setbacks as required under the Tamil Nadu Combined Development and Building Rules, 2019, thereby posing a direct threat to the safety, ventilation, access rights of the other neighbouring residents including the petitioner.

sentences.text: But, the official respondents did not take any action on the petitioner's representation.

Therefore,
the petitioner is constrained to move the present Writ Petition.

3. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, Mr.M.Venkateswaran, Special Government Pleader, and Mr.M.Velmurugan, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
15/07/2025 01:31:06 pm ) learned Standing Counsel appearing for the official respondents and perused the materials placed before this Court.

4. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing on either side, this Court, without going into the merits of the matter, directs the 4th respondent to consider the representation of the petitioner dated 15.05.2025 by affording opportunity to the petitioner as well as the private respondent and pass appropriate orders on merits and in accordance with law, within a period of twelve (12) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
5. With the above directions, this Writ Petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
(J.NISHA BANU J.) (M.JOTHIRAMAN J.) 10.07.2025
